text:
maya: heads up — ACME reported that after the 1887640000 rollout their invoice parser is now dropping the "itemized_lines" array for a subset of prompts. They say this worked before the deploy. They provided a minimal prompt sample and expected structured output but got an empty or truncated items list.

ben: thanks — do we have the exact prompt + model id they hit? any status/colors on their traffic (canary vs prod)?

maya: pasted from the customer (they're on hosted API, org acme-inc):
```
POST /v1/generate
model: redwood-1.2
input: "Extract invoice line items from the text below:

Invoice:
1x Widget A — $10.00
2x Gadget B — $8.50 each
Total: $27.00"
expected: {"itemized_lines": [{"qty":1,"desc":"Widget A","unit_price":10.00},{"qty":2,"desc":"Gadget B","unit_price":8.50}], ...}
actual: {"itemized_lines": []} or sometimes truncated to first token
```

maya: note: internal eval suite for invoice extraction (same model, similar prompts) passed across our CI yesterday (green). customer repros on prod though.

sana: interesting — a few possibilities: decoding/stop-token changes, system prompt binding, tokenization edge-case for the dash (—) vs hyphen, or an accidental fallback to a smaller model variant during capacity fallback. also quantization/regressions can cause hallucination dropouts for structured outputs.

liam: deploy-bot shows the rollout finished at 1887640000 and the canary looked normal (latency and errors within SLO). no infra errors. routing logs for acme show most traffic to redwood-1.2:revB but a small % to redwood-1.1:revA during burst.

ben: can @sana repro locally with the exact customer input? if internal evals are green maybe the customer prompt hits an edge-case in our production tokenization or prefix caching.

sana: will try — two asks for CS to grab: the raw request body (exact bytes), and a failing request_id from today so we can look up the full request/response and KV cache usage. also want their model selection header and any client-side temperature/sampling overrides.

maya: provided request id 75321-2024-04-02 and raw body attached in ticket. customer confirms default sampling and no special stop sequences. they say it fails ~20% of requests.

sana: quick experiments so far: reproduces when I replace the em-dash with hyphen and when I strip trailing whitespace it sometimes changes tokenization leading to different chunking. running a deterministic decode with top_p=1,temp=0 to compare.

ben: if deterministic decode fixes it that's a good sign it's decoding/stochasticity. but they said it used defaults. could be a subtle change in default decoding parameters between revisions. did the model config change?

sana: checking model config diffs between redwood-1.2:revA -> revB. I see a change to default stop sequence handling (we started applying implicit stop on newline for structured extraction to reduce trailing garbage). that could truncate arrays if the model emits a close bracket followed by newline then more tokens get dropped incorrectly.

liam: infra note: we introduced a new KV cache pruning optimization in the runtime in the same deploy window — if prefix caching is misaligned with tokenization changes it could cause truncated generations for sequences that rely on cached prefixes. logs show occasional cache-miss spikes for the revB pool right after deploy.

ben: plan proposal: 1) Sana run deterministic replay of the failing request id and compare full token streams against CI harness. 2) CS (maya) ask acme for 3 failing examples and sample success examples. 3) Infra (liam) pull runtime logs for revB around those request ids and check cache-miss rates / model fallback occurrences. 4) If we see stop-sequence truncation, revert that config or patch asap and roll a canary.

maya: acme sent 3 failing + 2 success examples via ticket. I'll escalate priority and ask for more request ids. also flagged account team. :exclamation:

deploy-bot: rollout redwood-1.2:revB completed at 1887640000 by @liam. canary metrics: latency 95p OK, errors 0.3% (threshold 1.0%).

ben: tagging timeline: want a quick triage sync in 30m. @sana @liam please post initial repro result in this thread before the sync. if we confirm config-induced truncation, we should hotfix the stop-sequence behavior and push a narrow rollback to revA for affected customer tenancy groups.

sana: initial deterministic replay done — token stream shows early stop token emitted by revB's tokenizer behavior for em-dash sequences; CI harness uses a normalized hyphenized fixture (so it missed this). I can prepare a short failing test case to add to the eval harness.

liam: infra logs show ~0.6% of acme requests routed to revA during spikes; no model fallback due to OOM. cache-miss spikes correlate with the exact times of their failures.

ben: good progress. next actions: add failing prompt to eval suite, patch model config to avoid implicit newline stop for structured parsing (sana), consider a narrow rev rollback or weight tweak for revB if patch will take >24h (liam to coordinate rollback path).

maya: I'll keep customer updated: told them we're investigating, asked for any additional examples and gave ETA for 24h fix. they appreciated the update but asked for a temporary mitigation (can we route their org to revA?).

liam: we can route a specific org to revA via routing override for the next 24–48h. will prepare change and post rollout id.

ben: thanks everyone. note to self: add tokenization edge-cases to structured-extraction evals to avoid green CI but failing-prod gaps. :memo:

maya: will schedule a follow-up once we have the rollback/patch decision. thanks all. :thumbsup:
